items.title: Heavy rain can more than double glacier speeds in Alaska
items.summary: Glaciers are often thought of as unyielding blocks of ice that slowly carve out the landscape as they move downhill by gravity. But sometimes their slow crawl becomes a surge that sees them move orders of magnitude faster than their usual speed.

items.title: The introduction of a medieval public health system exposed the population to roundworm
items.summary: Medieval health and sanitation efforts involved deliberate interventions; however, some of these measures had the opposite effect, leading to an increased spread of disease in Trondheim.

items.title: Why treating soil acidity crop by crop is no longer enough for prairie farmers
items.summary: To protect their future harvests, Western Canadian farmers need to manage soil acidity across their entire multiyear rotation rather than crop by crop, long-term research from the University of Alberta suggests.

items.title: Diwali celebrations coincide with worsening air. Here's how to stay safer
items.summary: For people across South Asia, especially in northern India, Diwali celebrations coincide with the return of hazardous winter air, raising concerns about how to celebrate safely.

items.title: Polar vortex faltering weeks earlier than ever recorded
items.summary: Meteorologists said Friday they were observing an unprecedented early disruption of the polar vortex, raising the risk of cold snaps across the Northern Hemisphere, though there remains significant uncertainty.

items.title: Pakistani astronaut to board Shenzhou 24 and become the first foreigner on China's space station
items.summary: A Pakistani astronaut will join the crew of China's Shenzhou 24 spacecraft on a mission that would make him the first foreign national to board Beijing's space station, state media reported Saturday.

items.title: Scientists discovered an unknown baby right whale off Canada. They say it's a cause for joy
items.summary: It would seem difficult to miss a 15,000-pound (6,804-kilogram) baby, but for months scientists who study rare whales did just that, and now they couldn't be happier.

items.title: Atlanta's new giant pandas will make their public debut after a 2-year absence
items.summary: Panda lovers are expected to line up Friday at Zoo Atlanta to see a new pair of giant pandas make their public debut.

items.title: Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk
items.summary: Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily was linked to a dramatically lower risk of dementia and better cognitive functioning in a study spanning up to 43 years. The benefits appeared regardless of genetic risk, but decaffeinated coffee did not show the same association.

items.title: Redefining honesty in a crisis: Why truth alone is not enough
items.summary: When a company suffers a cyberattack, leaks customer data or faces a major public scandal, telling the truth is essential. But new research suggests it is not enough on its own: organizations also need to communicate early, treat people with respect and show how they intend to put things right.
